chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadala ibn Ayyub, from al-Qasim ibn Burayd, from Malik al-Juhani, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Zakat al-Fitr, and he said: 'Give it to the Muslims; if you do not find a Muslim, then [give it to] the weak/poor, and give it to your relatives if you wish.'

key_terms.زَكَاةُ الْفِطْرَةِ: Zakat al-Fitr (alms of breaking the fast)

ai.seo_question: Who are the primary recipients of Zakat al-Fitr according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes a clear hierarchy for Zakat al-Fitr distribution, prioritizing the general Muslim community before moving to the needy, and finally allowing discretion for one's own relatives. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential view that while Zakat is primarily for the poor, it serves to strengthen communal bonds, with the option to give to kin emphasizing the dual spiritual and social benefits of charity. The chain of transmission through al-Tusi's Tahdhib underscores the reliability of this practice in early Shia legal tradition.
